value.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if x_K(W)⊆W, y_K(W)⊆W and h_K(W)⊆W, then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L_K-module, for every field K of characteristic p and every integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

hypotheses.statement: p is a prime integer, K is a field of characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight λ and of complex dimension λ+1.
The Chevalley generators satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h, both in sl2(C) and in the action on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊆V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. No equality with the minimal lattice is assumed.

definitions.type: family of complex linear operators on V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, X_r=x^r/r! in the universal enveloping algebra and in its action on V; X_0 is the identity.

definitions.type: family of complex linear operators on V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, Y_r=y^r/r! in the universal enveloping algebra and in its action on V; Y_0 is the identity.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl2(C)
definitions.definition: U_Z is the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra generated by all X_r and Y_r for integers r≥0; its action on V is the given enveloping-algebra action.

definitions.type: family of vectors in V indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i∈I, e_i=y^i v/i!=Y_i v.
R=Z_(p)={a/b∈Q:a,b∈Z and p does not divide b}. It is embedded in C through Q.
M_R=R⊗_Z M; tensors use the natural integer-module structures.

definitions.type: R-linear map from M_R to V
definitions.definition: μ:M_R→V is the multiplication map μ(r⊗m)=r m for r∈R,m∈M. Its image is the R-span of M inside V. Identification of M_R with that image is made only after proving injectivity.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I×I
definitions.definition: For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k∈I and k≠j to zero, using the previously proved basis (e_k) of V.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i∈I, J_i={c∈C:c e_i∈μ(M_R)}.
J=J_0, using 0∈I under the original nonnegative range of λ.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_Z K.
L_K=L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K, with bracket induced from [h,x]=2x,[h,y]=-2y,[x,y]=h. No assertion that this is a simple Lie algebra in characteristic 2 is made.
x_K(m⊗c)=(xm)⊗c, for m∈M,c∈K. Admissibility gives xM⊆M since x=X_1.
y_K(m⊗c)=(ym)⊗c, for m∈M,c∈K. Admissibility gives yM⊆M since y=Y_1.
h_K=x_K y_K-y_K x_K.

3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an

value.representation_notes: Use one complex vector space V and its three Chevalley endomorphisms. H003 is the action of the standard sl2 presentation, H002 retains finite dimension, irreducibility and existence of a highest-weight vector, and H004 supplies the chosen vector. The omitted explicit LieModule bundle is determined uniquely by these three generator actions and their brackets; no result uses a different complex representation. M is a ℤ-submodule, equivalently an additive subgroup. Admissibility is a finite integer basis whose ambient images form a complex basis plus stability under every divided power, equivalent to U_Z stability. p:ℕ represents the positive prime integer and lam:ℤ is unchanged. H001 contains primality, characteristic and 0≤lam<p. Every use of toNat is guarded by that nonnegative hypothesis; Fin(lam.toNat+1) corresponds bijectively to the integer interval I. All exponents r,d use ℕ, equivalent to nonnegative integers. R is implemented as the subring closure of fractions with denominator prime to p; T005 proves this closure has exactly that carrier before relying on its localization meaning. MR=R⊗ℤM; mu is the multiplication lift, and image is used only with proved injectivity. Ji is the inverse image of mu(MR) under c↦c e_i, not an assumed rank-one submodule. VK is K⊗ℤM consistently throughout, using the canonical tensor flip from the source M⊗ℤK; no additional vector-space model is introduced. latticeOp is the restriction when its Stable guard holds and zero otherwise; H005 and the bracket identity prove the guards before it is used as an induced action, explicitly exported in N005. kop is its scalar extension. Module.End multiplication is composition with the right factor first, powers are iterated operators, and kdp is the inverse factorial scalar multiple. Basis coordinate maps define unit B i j: w↦(j-th coordinate of w) B_i. Actions uses integer casts into the coefficient field; basisAt extends a finite basis by zero and uses predecessor/successor only under the source boundary guards. Output predicates abbreviate full displayed propositions and assume none of their clauses. Background notes remain local references; M001 is applied directly from the pinned library at T009 and is not a premise port.

steps.statement: Strings lam x y h v
steps.explanation: Prove the two commutator recurrences by natural induction; d≥1 is a guard on the x formula. Nonnegative integer exponents use ℕ with its canonical identification with the source range.

steps.statement: Coordinates lam y v
steps.explanation: Show e_i≠0 by the iterated raising formula. Isolate coefficients with the product of h minus the other complex eigenvalues, then use finite dimension. Fin(lam.toNat+1) enumerates exactly the integer interval I under H001.

steps.statement: ∀ d : ℕ, lam < (d : ℤ) → (y ^ d) v = 0
steps.explanation: Use the e-basis spectrum to kill y^(lam+1)v at the absent complex weight, then all higher powers. No reduction of weights.

steps.statement: ComplexOutput lam x y h v
steps.explanation: N001: derive the x,y,h coordinate formulas, iterate and divide by factorials to obtain both integral binomial formulas including out-of-range zero cases; package all earlier clauses.

steps.statement: LocalBasics p lam M x y
steps.explanation: Prove the closure-based R equals the source rational local ring; this is a representation obligation, not an assumption. Extend an admissible integer basis to R, prove μ injective by its complex independence, and prove spanning and divided-power preservation/intertwining on pure tensors. Basis.baseChange and LinearMap.liftBaseChange implement these maps.

steps.statement: MatrixOutput p lam M x y v
steps.explanation: N002: compute Q and the three matrix-unit factors on the e-basis. Prove the binomial integers are units in R using factorial divisibility below p, then show their compositions preserve μ(M_R). Multiplication of endomorphisms applies the right factor first, as in Module.End.mul_apply.

steps.statement: CommonOutput p lam M x y v
steps.explanation: N003: coordinate projections give finitely generated J_i; matrix units identify them all and spanning proves nonzero. The displayed equivalence J^I≃M_R must have the exact coordinate-sum formula after μ. Prove bijectivity using the complex e-basis and μ injectivity; do not assume J has rational rank one.

steps.statement: FractionData p M y v
steps.explanation: Use the rational fraction field of R. Construct multiplication theta and prove injectivity by a common nonzero denominator. Tensor a finite R-generating family to prove finite dimensionality. Establish any needed scalar-tower compatibility locally from the explicitly defined embeddings; it is not a new premise.

steps.statement: RationalLine p M y v
steps.explanation: Tensor the coordinate equivalence and a finite R-basis to get n=nr with n>0. Use Module.finrank_pi_fintype directly at ℚ, finite I, constant family T; finite dimensionality supplies freeness and finite generation, and ℚ supplies StrongRankCondition. Through injective theta obtain the unique rational ratio.

steps.statement: PrincipalOutput p lam M y v
steps.explanation: N004: choose a nonzero a and finite nonempty generating family of nonzero members of J. Express each rational ratio as p^d times a unit of R by integer p-factor extraction. Choose the minimum exponent, prove J=Rb and construct the R-basis mapping to b e_i. Private choices remain local; the export is existence of b and the prescribed basis.

steps.statement: ScalarExtensionData p K M
steps.explanation: Construct the characteristic-p fraction map rho and kernel pR, then the two natural scalar-extension equivalences with the displayed pure-tensor formulas. Tensor factors consistently put the scalar ring first. Check balancing, inverses and naturality on pure tensors. The ZMod p action on M_R/pM_R is constructed here. H001 provides CharP only as a proposition; install it locally, without assuming extra instances globally.

steps.statement: ReducedBasisData p K lam M x y h v
steps.explanation: Extend the R-basis b e_i along rho and transport by phi inverse. Basis.baseChange gives 1⊗BR_i, proving independence as well as spanning. The integer matrices from N001 transport through μ and phi. Export the exact same rho, phi, scalar b, R-basis BR and K-basis B with pure-tensor and naturality formulas: these witnesses are needed for the next matrix-unit transport, not merely a basis with matching three matrices.

steps.statement: ReducedOutput K lam M x y h
steps.explanation: N005: take the compatible witnesses from T012. Prove factorials through λ are nonzero in K and identify induced divided powers with inverse-factorial powers by tensoring r!X_r=x^r. N002's matrix-unit operators, their R-unit coefficients, μ injectivity and the prescribed b e_i R-basis show after extension by the same rho and phi that they become unit B i j. This proves the displayed K matrix-unit identity. Prove the induced brackets from H003 and lattice stability and assemble every N005 clause, without comparing reduced weights.

steps.statement:
Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
  ∀ (B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) K (VK K M)),
    (∀ i j : Fin (lam.toNat + 1), (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧
      unit B i j = ((Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : K)⁻¹) •
        (kdp (kop K M x) (lam.toNat - i.val) * kdp (kop K M y) lam.toNat *
         kdp (kop K M x) lam.toNat * kdp (kop K M y) (lam.toNat - j.val))) →
    ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M), Inv W (kop K M x) → Inv W (kop K M y) →
      Inv W (kop K M h) → ∀ i j, Inv W (unit B i j)
steps.explanation: N005 gives a nonempty finite basis and hence nontriviality. Invariance under x_K and y_K gives invariance under powers, scalar multiples and compositions, so under every displayed matrix unit. Keep W arbitrary and its invariance hypotheses scoped in the implication.

steps.statement:
∀ (B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) K (VK K M))
  (W : Submodule K (VK K M)), W ≠ ⊥ →
  ∃ w : VK K M, w ∈ W ∧ w ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ j : Fin (lam.toNat + 1), B.repr w j ≠ 0
steps.explanation: For a nonzero subspace choose a nonzero vector. Its finite basis coordinates cannot all vanish. The witness is local to this existence result and eliminated only in the final step.

steps.statement: Target K M x y h
steps.explanation: P: split W=⊥ or W≠⊥. In the latter case choose a nonzero coefficient, apply each T_ij and divide by that coefficient to place every basis vector in W. Thus W=⊤. Combine with nontriviality. The explicit induced brackets in N005 ensure invariance under these generators is precisely invariance for the Chevalley L_K action, including p=2. No algebraic-closure assumption or distinct reduced weights enter.

source_steps.text: By H003 and H004, h y^0v=λv. For the h-identity, assume the induction hypothesis L1: hy^d v=(λ-2d)y^dv. Then hy^(d+1)v=(yh-2y)y^dv=(λ-2d-2)y^(d+1)v. Discharging L1 and using induction proves the h-identity for every d≥0. Also xyv=(yx+h)v=λv. For the x-identity, at an arbitrary d≥1 assume L2: xy^dv=d(λ-d+1)y^(d-1)v. The just proved h-identity gives xy^(d+1)v=(yx+h)y^dv=[d(λ-d+1)+λ-2d]y^dv=(d+1)(λ-d)y^dv. Discharging L2 and inducting from d=1 proves the x-identity. The d=0 x-value is xv=0. These are identities of complex vectors; no reduction of weights has occurred.

H001 implies n>0 and |I|=λ+1=n. Iterating F001 gives x^i y^iv=i!·λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v for i∈I. Every factor in this product is nonzero over C when i≥1, and the i=0 product is one; H004 therefore gives e_i≠0. Also he_i=(λ-2i)e_i by F001. The eigenvalues λ-2i are pairwise distinct over C. Assume L3: Σ_{i∈I}α_i e_i=0. For arbitrary j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id_V). All terms except the j-th vanish, leaving α_j·(∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k-j))e_j=0. Its vector and scalar product are nonzero (empty product one), so α_j=0. Discharge L3: every relation is trivial. There are n independent vectors and dim_C V=n by H002, hence they form a basis.

F001 at d=λ+1 gives h y^(λ+1)v=(-λ-2)y^(λ+1)v. Expanding this vector in the basis F002, the equation says that its coefficient at every e_i is killed by (λ-2i)-(-λ-2)=2(λ+1-i), nonzero over C for i∈I. Thus y^(λ+1)v=0; equivalently a nonzero vector of this eigenvalue would contradict the basis spectrum. Applying further powers of y gives y^dv=0 for all d>λ.

For i∈I the definitions and F001 give xe_0=0 and xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1) for i≥1. They also give ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 by F003, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. Iterating these formulas r times and dividing by r! yields X_r e_i=[(λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!]e_(i-r)=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) for r≤i, and Y_r e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_(i+r)=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) for i+r≤λ. The products are empty when r=0. Otherwise the x-string reaches e_0 and is killed, or the y-string passes e_λ and is killed, so the remaining cases give zero. These coefficients are integers by the usual finite binomial formula. Together with F001–F003 this proves every clause of the output.

Choose the basis m from H005. It has n members because it and the N001 basis are both complex bases of V. The tensors of its members with 1 give an R-basis of R⊗_Z M: the integer coordinate maps extend to inverse R-coordinate maps, exhibiting the isomorphism with R^n. Under μ a tensor has these same coordinates as a complex linear combination of the members of m, so complex independence makes μ injective. Its image contains M and therefore spans V over C. Admissibility in H005 gives X_r M,Y_r M⊆M for every r≥0. Extending each operator R-linearly preserves M_R and commutes with μ. From now on identify M_R with its image.

Define Q=Y_λ X_λ. On the basis N001, X_λ kills every e_k except e_λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Hence Q=E_(λλ), and X_(λ-i)Q=E_(iλ), again with coefficient binom(λ-i,λ-i)=1. Also QY_(λ-j)=binom(λ,j)E_(λj): an input index below j lands below e_λ and is killed by Q; an input above j passes the end of the lowering string; the input e_j has coefficient binom(λ,λ-j)=binom(λ,j). Since 0≤j≤λ

For arbitrary i,j∈I, F002 gives binom(λ,j)^(-1)X_(λ-i)QY_(λ-j)=E_(iλ)E_(λj)=E_ij, as can also be checked on every basis vector. Substituting Q=Y_λ X_λ yields the asserted identity. Each factor preserves M_R by F001, and the scalar inverse belongs to R by F002; hence every E_ij preserves M_R. No comparison of weights modulo p is used.

By H001, 0∈I and n>0. Use the injection and identification in N002. For each i∈I, E_ii maps M_R onto J_i e_i: its image is contained there by coordinate projection, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. This image is finitely generated because the images of the n members of an R-basis of M_R generate it. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication by e_i identifies J_i with J_i e_i, so J_i is finitely generated. If c∈J_j, then c e_j∈M_R and E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i∈M_R by N002; hence J_j⊆J_i. Reversing i,j proves equality, and each equals J_0=J. At least one coordinate image is nonzero, since otherwise M_R would be zero, contradicting that its complex span is the nonzero V with n>0. Thus the common J is nonzero.

Each vector of M_R is the sum of its coordinate projections E_ii, so F001 places it in Σ_{i∈I}J e_i. Conversely each of these coordinate submodules is contained in M_R by definition. The sum is direct because (e_i) is a complex basis by N001: a relation Σc_i e_i=0 with c_i∈J⊆C forces every coefficient to vanish. Thus the coordinate-sum map J^I→M_R is an R-linear bijection, with inverse given by its coordinates. N001 supplies n>0 and the basis of V, and N002 supplies injectivity, rank n and complex spanning, giving all the other exported clauses.

By N003, J⊆C is finitely generated and nonzero, and M_R is free of rank n with coordinate decomposition J^I. Define T=Q⊗_R J and θ(q⊗c)=qc. The fraction field of R is Q: integers lie in R and every rational is a quotient of two elements of R with nonzero denominator. To see the multiplication map is injective, write any finite tensor sum over a common nonzero denominator s∈R as (1/s)⊗c with c∈J. If θ sends it to zero then c/s=0 in C, so c=0, and the tensor is zero. This also gives the usual identification of this tensor product with the localization of J. A finite R-generating family of J yields a finite Q-spanning family of T by tensoring; consequently T is finite dimensional. This proves the localization injectivity used here without presuming that containment J⊆C implies rank one.

Set r=dim_Q T. Tensor the R-coordinate isomorphism in N003 with Q. The result is a Q-linear isomorphism Q⊗_R M_R≅T^I: tensor the coordinate maps in each direction, and identify Q⊗_R J^I with T^I by q⊗(c_i)_i↦(q⊗c_i)_i, whose inverse sums the tensors supported at one coordinate. Finite I makes these mutually inverse. An R-basis of M_R of n members, supplied by N003, extends to a Q-basis of Q⊗_R M_R; its coefficient maps extend and prove both spanning and independence. Its dimension is therefore n. Apply M001 to the finite product T^I over Q: F001 gives finite dimension, hence a finite basis and finite generation; Q has the strong rank condition by the usual finite independent-family bound. M001 gives dim_Q T^I=Σ_{i∈I}dim_Q T=nr, using |I|=n. Thus n=nr, so r=1 because n>0 by N003. By F001, θ identifies T with a one-dimensional rational subspace of C containing J. In particular, for any nonzero a∈J and any c∈J there is a unique q∈Q with c=qa.

Choose 0≠a∈J and a nonempty finite generating family g of nonzero elements of J using N003. By F002, write its members as g_j=q_j a with q_j∈Q×. For each such rational q_j, removing all powers of the prime p from its nonzero integer numerator and denominator gives q_j=p^{d_j}u_j, where d_j∈Z and both u_j and u_j^(-1) lie in R: neither the remaining numerator nor denominator is divisible by p. This is just finite factorization by repeated division of nonzero integers by p, and works for positive or negative exponents and signs. The resulting finite family of integer exponents is nonempty.

Let d be the family of exponents from F003 and set u_j=p^(-d_j)q_j, a unit of R for each index j. Let ν=min_j d_j and define b=p^ν a. Since p is prime and a≠0, b≠0. For every generator q_j a, its ratio to b is p^{d_j-ν}u_j∈R because d_j≥ν. Thus J⊆Rb. For an index attaining the minimum, q_j a=u_j b and u_j is a unit, so b=u_j^(-1)q_j a∈J. Hence Rb⊆J and J=Rb. Finally the decomposition M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i from N003 becomes M_R=⊕_{i∈I}R b e_i. These vectors span, and are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex independent. They therefore form an R-basis. Export only existence of such b, discharging the private choices a,g,q and their identities.

Every integer denominator of an element of R is prime to p, so its image in the characteristic-p field K is nonzero by H001. Thus ρ:R→K, ρ(a/b)=ā b̄^(-1), is a well-defined ring map; equality of fractions and the ring laws follow by cross multiplication. Its kernel is pR and its residue field is Z/pZ: ρ(a/b)=0 exactly when p divides a. Define φ: M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse takes (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. Both maps respect all tensor balancing relations and are inverse on pure tensors, which span. Also η:z⊗c↦(z mod pM_R)⊗c identifies M_R⊗_R K with (M_R/pM_R)⊗_(Z/pZ)K. The inverse sends (z mod pM_R)⊗c to z⊗c; changing z by p times a vector gives zero because pK=0, and all remaining balancing relations follow from ρ. These are the two natural isomorphisms of the supplied proof. H005 gives xM,yM⊆M and H003 gives h=xy-yx, hence hM⊆M. Tensoring these lattice operators commutes with φ and η by their formulas. The induced h equals h_K=x_Ky_K-y_Kx_K. The induced brackets therefore give the L_K-action, including characteristic 2.

Choose b from N004 and define B_i=φ^(-1)((b e_i)⊗1). The R-coordinate isomorphism M_R≅R^I given by the basis (b e_i) tensors to K^I; tensoring its coordinate maps gives inverse coefficient maps, proving that B is a K-basis, not merely a spanning family. Alternatively its reduction is a basis of M_R/pM_R over Z/pZ and then extends to K, via F001. N001 gives the matrices of x,y,h on e_i, and complex linearity gives the same matrices on b e_i. Their coefficients are integers, so extension along ρ and transport by φ give exactly x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for i≥1, y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for i<λ, y_K B_λ=0, and h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i, with integer coefficients read in K. Also n>0 by N001.

For every r with 0≤r≤λ<p, none of 1,...,r is divisible by p, so r! is nonzero in K by H001. Define A_r=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and C_r=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. On M the identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold; all these operators preserve M by H005. After extension they show that the induced X_r,Y_r are exactly A_r,C_r. For i,j∈I, N002 expresses E_ij as a composition of R-lattice operators and the unit binom(λ,j)^(-1). Its extension, transported by φ, sends B_j to B_i and every other B-coordinate to zero, hence is the map T_ij defined from F002. The image of that unit under ρ remains a unit and is the inverse of the coefficient binom(λ,j) in K, so this coefficient is nonzero. Substituting the just established induced divided powers in N002 gives T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) A_(λ-i) C_λ A_λ C_(λ-j). This proves every exported clause of the output without comparing reduced weights.

By N005 choose B and its matrix units T. There are n=λ+1>0 basis vectors, so V_K≠0. Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. Invariance under x_K and y_K implies invariance under their nonnegative powers and scalar multiples, so under every A_r,C_r in N005. Composing these operators and multiplying by binom(λ,j)^(-1) shows, using the N005 identity, that every T_ij preserves W. This assertion holds for all i,j∈I. By classical cases W=0 or W≠0. Under the zero branch L3: W=0, the desired disjunction holds immediately, and L3 is discharged. In the remaining branch assume L2: W≠0; then there exists a nonzero vector of W.
Choose 0≠w∈W using F001 and expand w=Σ_{i∈I}c_i B_i in the basis N005. If every c_i were zero then the expansion would give w=0, a contradiction. Thus there exists an index j∈I with c_j≠0.

Choose such j by F002. For arbitrary i∈I, the matrix-unit definition gives T_ij w=c_j B_i. By F001 this vector is in W, and c_j is invertible in the field K. Hence B_i=c_j^(-1)T_ij w∈W. All basis vectors belong to W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 and combine with the zero branch to obtain W=0 or W=V_K under L1. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. By N005 the operators are the induced lattice actions, and by H003 the integer span of x,y,h is closed under bracket; the induced action is the stated L_K-action. Its invariant subspaces are exactly the subspaces invariant under these three generators. H005 ensures these are the actions on the original arbitrary lattice tensor product V_K. Finally H001 permits λ=0 (all factorials and binomial coefficients used equal one) and permits p=2 with λ=0 or 1. None of the argument required distinct h_K eigenvalues or algebraic closure of K. This proves P in the full original domain.

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.
183:

6: def R (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
7:   Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
8: instance ratModule (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module ℚ V :=
9:   Module.compHom V (algebraMap ℚ ℂ)
10: instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=

12: instance localModule (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V :=
13:   Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
14: variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
15: def dp (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
16:   ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
17: def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := dp y i v
18: abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := (R p) ⊗[ℤ] M
19: def mu (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
20:   M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
21: abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
22: def image (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
23:   LinearMap.range (mu p M)
24: def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
25:   letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
26:   letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ ℂ := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ ℂ
27:   (image p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
28: def unit {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
29:     {n : ℕ} (B : Module.Basis (Fin n) F W) (i j : Fin n) : Module.End F W :=
30:   (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton F W (B i)).comp (B.coord j)
31: def basisAt {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
32:     {n : ℕ} (B : Module.Basis (Fin n) F W) (i : ℕ) : W :=
33:   if hi : i < n then B ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
34: def Stable (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
35:   ∀ w ∈ M, f w ∈ M
36: def latticeOp (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End ℤ M :=
37:   letI := Classical.propDecidable

39: def kop (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End K (VK K M) :=
40:   (latticeOp M f).baseChange K
41: def kdp {K W : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W]
42:     (f : Module.End K W) (r : ℕ) : Module.End K W :=

44: def Coordinates (lam : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
45:   ∃ B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) ℂ V, ∀ i, B i = e y v i.val
46: def rop (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End (R p) (MR p M) :=
47:   (latticeOp M f).baseChange (R p)
48: def pSub (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) (MR p M) :=
49:   Submodule.span (R p) (Set.range (fun z : MR p M => (p : R p) • z))
50: abbrev QuotMR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := MR p M ⧸ pSub p M
51: def Inv {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
52:     (W' : Submodule F W) (f : Module.End F W) : Prop :=

54: def Actions {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]

56:   (∀ i, a (B i) = if i.val = 0 then 0 else

60:   (∀ i, c (B i) = ((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • B i)

64:     (((d : ℤ) * (lam - (d : ℤ) + 1) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ (d - 1)) v)

value.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if x_K(W)⊆W, y_K(W)⊆W and h_K(W)⊆W, then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L_K-module, for every field K of characteristic p and every integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

hypotheses.statement: p is a prime integer, K is a field of characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight λ and of complex dimension λ+1.
The Chevalley generators satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h, both in sl2(C) and in the action on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊆V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. No equality with the minimal lattice is assumed.

definitions.type: family of complex linear operators on V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, X_r=x^r/r! in the universal enveloping algebra and in its action on V; X_0 is the identity.

definitions.type: family of complex linear operators on V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, Y_r=y^r/r! in the universal enveloping algebra and in its action on V; Y_0 is the identity.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl2(C)
definitions.definition: U_Z is the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra generated by all X_r and Y_r for integers r≥0; its action on V is the given enveloping-algebra action.

definitions.type: family of vectors in V indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i∈I, e_i=y^i v/i!=Y_i v.
R=Z_(p)={a/b∈Q:a,b∈Z and p does not divide b}. It is embedded in C through Q.
M_R=R⊗_Z M; tensors use the natural integer-module structures.

definitions.type: R-linear map from M_R to V
definitions.definition: μ:M_R→V is the multiplication map μ(r⊗m)=r m for r∈R,m∈M. Its image is the R-span of M inside V. Identification of M_R with that image is made only after proving injectivity.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I×I
definitions.definition: For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k∈I and k≠j to zero, using the previously proved basis (e_k) of V.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i∈I, J_i={c∈C:c e_i∈μ(M_R)}.
J=J_0, using 0∈I under the original nonnegative range of λ.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_Z K.
L_K=L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K, with bracket induced from [h,x]=2x,[h,y]=-2y,[x,y]=h. No assertion that this is a simple Lie algebra in characteristic 2 is made.
x_K(m⊗c)=(xm)⊗c, for m∈M,c∈K. Admissibility gives xM⊆M since x=X_1.
y_K(m⊗c)=(ym)⊗c, for m∈M,c∈K. Admissibility gives yM⊆M since y=Y_1.
h_K=x_K y_K-y_K x_K.

value.representation_notes: Use one complex vector space V and its three Chevalley endomorphisms. H003 is the action of the standard sl2 presentation, H002 retains finite dimension, irreducibility and existence of a highest-weight vector, and H004 supplies the chosen vector. The omitted explicit LieModule bundle is determined uniquely by these three generator actions and their brackets; no result uses a different complex representation. M is a ℤ-submodule, equivalently an additive subgroup. Admissibility is a finite integer basis whose ambient images form a complex basis plus stability under every divided power, equivalent to U_Z stability. p:ℕ represents the positive prime integer and lam:ℤ is unchanged. H001 contains primality, characteristic and 0≤lam<p. Every use of toNat is guarded by that nonnegative hypothesis; Fin(lam.toNat+1) corresponds bijectively to the integer interval I. All exponents r,d use ℕ, equivalent to nonnegative integers. R is implemented as the subring closure of fractions with denominator prime to p; T005 proves this closure has exactly that carrier before relying on its localization meaning. MR=R⊗ℤM; mu is the multiplication lift, and image is used only with proved injectivity. Ji is the inverse image of mu(MR) under c↦c e_i, not an assumed rank-one submodule. VK is K⊗ℤM consistently throughout, using the canonical tensor flip from the source M⊗ℤK; no additional vector-space model is introduced. latticeOp is the restriction when its Stable guard holds and zero otherwise; H005 and the bracket identity prove the guards before it is used as an induced action, explicitly exported in N005. kop is its scalar extension. Module.End multiplication is composition with the right factor first, powers are iterated operators, and kdp is the inverse factorial scalar multiple. Basis coordinate maps define unit B i j: w↦(j-th coordinate of w) B_i. Actions uses integer casts into the coefficient field; basisAt extends a finite basis by zero and uses predecessor/successor only under the source boundary guards. Output predicates abbreviate full displayed propositions and assume none of their clauses. Background notes remain local references; M001 is applied directly from the pinned library at T009 and is not a premise port.

steps.statement: Strings lam x y h v
steps.explanation: Prove the two commutator recurrences by natural induction; d≥1 is a guard on the x formula. Nonnegative integer exponents use ℕ with its canonical identification with the source range.

steps.statement: Coordinates lam y v
steps.explanation: Show e_i≠0 by the iterated raising formula. Isolate coefficients with the product of h minus the other complex eigenvalues, then use finite dimension. Fin(lam.toNat+1) enumerates exactly the integer interval I under H001.

steps.statement: ∀ d : ℕ, lam < (d : ℤ) → (y ^ d) v = 0
steps.explanation: Use the e-basis spectrum to kill y^(lam+1)v at the absent complex weight, then all higher powers. No reduction of weights.

steps.statement: ComplexOutput lam x y h v
steps.explanation: N001: derive the x,y,h coordinate formulas, iterate and divide by factorials to obtain both integral binomial formulas including out-of-range zero cases; package all earlier clauses.

steps.statement: LocalBasics p lam M x y
steps.explanation: Prove the closure-based R equals the source rational local ring; this is a representation obligation, not an assumption. Extend an admissible integer basis to R, prove μ injective by its complex independence, and prove spanning and divided-power preservation/intertwining on pure tensors. Basis.baseChange and LinearMap.liftBaseChange implement these maps.

steps.statement: MatrixOutput p lam M x y v
steps.explanation: N002: compute Q and the three matrix-unit factors on the e-basis. Prove the binomial integers are units in R using factorial divisibility below p, then show their compositions preserve μ(M_R). Multiplication of endomorphisms applies the right factor first, as in Module.End.mul_apply.

steps.statement: CommonOutput p lam M x y v
steps.explanation: N003: coordinate projections give finitely generated J_i; matrix units identify them all and spanning proves nonzero. The displayed equivalence J^I≃M_R must have the exact coordinate-sum formula after μ. Prove bijectivity using the complex e-basis and μ injectivity; do not assume J has rational rank one.

steps.statement: FractionData p M y v
steps.explanation: Use the rational fraction field of R. Construct multiplication theta and prove injectivity by a common nonzero denominator. Tensor a finite R-generating family to prove finite dimensionality. Establish any needed scalar-tower compatibility locally from the explicitly defined embeddings; it is not a new premise.

steps.statement: RationalLine p M y v
steps.explanation: Tensor the coordinate equivalence and a finite R-basis to get n=nr with n>0. Use Module.finrank_pi_fintype directly at ℚ, finite I, constant family T; finite dimensionality supplies freeness and finite generation, and ℚ supplies StrongRankCondition. Through injective theta obtain the unique rational ratio.

steps.statement: PrincipalOutput p lam M y v
steps.explanation: N004: choose a nonzero a and finite nonempty generating family of nonzero members of J. Express each rational ratio as p^d times a unit of R by integer p-factor extraction. Choose the minimum exponent, prove J=Rb and construct the R-basis mapping to b e_i. Private choices remain local; the export is existence of b and the prescribed basis.

steps.statement: ScalarExtensionData p K M
steps.explanation: Construct the characteristic-p fraction map rho and kernel pR, then the two natural scalar-extension equivalences with the displayed pure-tensor formulas. Tensor factors consistently put the scalar ring first. Check balancing, inverses and naturality on pure tensors. The ZMod p action on M_R/pM_R is constructed here. H001 provides CharP only as a proposition; install it locally, without assuming extra instances globally.

steps.statement: ReducedBasisData p K lam M x y h v
steps.explanation: Extend the R-basis b e_i along rho and transport by phi inverse. Basis.baseChange gives 1⊗BR_i, proving independence as well as spanning. The integer matrices from N001 transport through μ and phi. Export the exact same rho, phi, scalar b, R-basis BR and K-basis B with pure-tensor and naturality formulas: these witnesses are needed for the next matrix-unit transport, not merely a basis with matching three matrices.

steps.statement: ReducedOutput K lam M x y h
steps.explanation: N005: take the compatible witnesses from T012. Prove factorials through λ are nonzero in K and identify induced divided powers with inverse-factorial powers by tensoring r!X_r=x^r. N002's matrix-unit operators, their R-unit coefficients, μ injectivity and the prescribed b e_i R-basis show after extension by the same rho and phi that they become unit B i j. This proves the displayed K matrix-unit identity. Prove the induced brackets from H003 and lattice stability and assemble every N005 clause, without comparing reduced weights.

steps.explanation: N005 gives a nonempty finite basis and hence nontriviality. Invariance under x_K and y_K gives invariance under powers, scalar multiples and compositions, so under every displayed matrix unit. Keep W arbitrary and its invariance hypotheses scoped in the implication.

steps.statement:
∀ (B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) K (VK K M))
  (W : Submodule K (VK K M)), W ≠ ⊥ →
  ∃ w : VK K M, w ∈ W ∧ w ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ j : Fin (lam.toNat + 1), B.repr w j ≠ 0
steps.explanation: For a nonzero subspace choose a nonzero vector. Its finite basis coordinates cannot all vanish. The witness is local to this existence result and eliminated only in the final step.

steps.statement: Target K M x y h
steps.explanation: P: split W=⊥ or W≠⊥. In the latter case choose a nonzero coefficient, apply each T_ij and divide by that coefficient to place every basis vector in W. Thus W=⊤. Combine with nontriviality. The explicit induced brackets in N005 ensure invariance under these generators is precisely invariance for the Chevalley L_K action, including p=2. No algebraic-closure assumption or distinct reduced weights enter.

source_steps.text: By H003 and H004, h y^0v=λv. For the h-identity, assume the induction hypothesis L1: hy^d v=(λ-2d)y^dv. Then hy^(d+1)v=(yh-2y)y^dv=(λ-2d-2)y^(d+1)v. Discharging L1 and using induction proves the h-identity for every d≥0. Also xyv=(yx+h)v=λv. For the x-identity, at an arbitrary d≥1 assume L2: xy^dv=d(λ-d+1)y^(d-1)v. The just proved h-identity gives xy^(d+1)v=(yx+h)y^dv=[d(λ-d+1)+λ-2d]y^dv=(d+1)(λ-d)y^dv. Discharging L2 and inducting from d=1 proves the x-identity. The d=0 x-value is xv=0. These are identities of complex vectors; no reduction of weights has occurred.

H001 implies n>0 and |I|=λ+1=n. Iterating F001 gives x^i y^iv=i!·λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v for i∈I. Every factor in this product is nonzero over C when i≥1, and the i=0 product is one; H004 therefore gives e_i≠0. Also he_i=(λ-2i)e_i by F001. The eigenvalues λ-2i are pairwise distinct over C. Assume L3: Σ_{i∈I}α_i e_i=0. For arbitrary j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id_V). All terms except the j-th vanish, leaving α_j·(∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k-j))e_j=0. Its vector and scalar product are nonzero (empty product one), so α_j=0. Discharge L3: every relation is trivial. There are n independent vectors and dim_C V=n by H002, hence they form a basis.

F001 at d=λ+1 gives h y^(λ+1)v=(-λ-2)y^(λ+1)v. Expanding this vector in the basis F002, the equation says that its coefficient at every e_i is killed by (λ-2i)-(-λ-2)=2(λ+1-i), nonzero over C for i∈I. Thus y^(λ+1)v=0; equivalently a nonzero vector of this eigenvalue would contradict the basis spectrum. Applying further powers of y gives y^dv=0 for all d>λ.

For i∈I the definitions and F001 give xe_0=0 and xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1) for i≥1. They also give ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 by F003, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. Iterating these formulas r times and dividing by r! yields X_r e_i=[(λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!]e_(i-r)=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) for r≤i, and Y_r e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_(i+r)=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) for i+r≤λ. The products are empty when r=0. Otherwise the x-string reaches e_0 and is killed, or the y-string passes e_λ and is killed, so the remaining cases give zero. These coefficients are integers by the usual finite binomial formula. Together with F001–F003 this proves every clause of the output.

Choose the basis m from H005. It has n members because it and the N001 basis are both complex bases of V. The tensors of its members with 1 give an R-basis of R⊗_Z M: the integer coordinate maps extend to inverse R-coordinate maps, exhibiting the isomorphism with R^n. Under μ a tensor has these same coordinates as a complex linear combination of the members of m, so complex independence makes μ injective. Its image contains M and therefore spans V over C. Admissibility in H005 gives X_r M,Y_r M⊆M for every r≥0. Extending each operator R-linearly preserves M_R and commutes with μ. From now on identify M_R with its image.

Define Q=Y_λ X_λ. On the basis N001, X_λ kills every e_k except e_λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Hence Q=E_(λλ), and X_(λ-i)Q=E_(iλ), again with coefficient binom(λ-i,λ-i)=1. Also QY_(λ-j)=binom(λ,j)E_(λj): an input index below j lands below e_λ and is killed by Q; an input above j passes the end of the lowering string; the input e_j has coefficient binom(λ,λ-j)=binom(λ,j). Since 0≤j≤λ

For arbitrary i,j∈I, F002 gives binom(λ,j)^(-1)X_(λ-i)QY_(λ-j)=E_(iλ)E_(λj)=E_ij, as can also be checked on every basis vector. Substituting Q=Y_λ X_λ yields the asserted identity. Each factor preserves M_R by F001, and the scalar inverse belongs to R by F002; hence every E_ij preserves M_R. No comparison of weights modulo p is used.

By H001, 0∈I and n>0. Use the injection and identification in N002. For each i∈I, E_ii maps M_R onto J_i e_i: its image is contained there by coordinate projection, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. This image is finitely generated because the images of the n members of an R-basis of M_R generate it. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication by e_i identifies J_i with J_i e_i, so J_i is finitely generated. If c∈J_j, then c e_j∈M_R and E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i∈M_R by N002; hence J_j⊆J_i. Reversing i,j proves equality, and each equals J_0=J. At least one coordinate image is nonzero, since otherwise M_R would be zero, contradicting that its complex span is the nonzero V with n>0. Thus the common J is nonzero.

Each vector of M_R is the sum of its coordinate projections E_ii, so F001 places it in Σ_{i∈I}J e_i. Conversely each of these coordinate submodules is contained in M_R by definition. The sum is direct because (e_i) is a complex basis by N001: a relation Σc_i e_i=0 with c_i∈J⊆C forces every coefficient to vanish. Thus the coordinate-sum map J^I→M_R is an R-linear bijection, with inverse given by its coordinates. N001 supplies n>0 and the basis of V, and N002 supplies injectivity, rank n and complex spanning, giving all the other exported clauses.

By N003, J⊆C is finitely generated and nonzero, and M_R is free of rank n with coordinate decomposition J^I. Define T=Q⊗_R J and θ(q⊗c)=qc. The fraction field of R is Q: integers lie in R and every rational is a quotient of two elements of R with nonzero denominator. To see the multiplication map is injective, write any finite tensor sum over a common nonzero denominator s∈R as (1/s)⊗c with c∈J. If θ sends it to zero then c/s=0 in C, so c=0, and the tensor is zero. This also gives the usual identification of this tensor product with the localization of J. A finite R-generating family of J yields a finite Q-spanning family of T by tensoring; consequently T is finite dimensional. This proves the localization injectivity used here without presuming that containment J⊆C implies rank one.

Set r=dim_Q T. Tensor the R-coordinate isomorphism in N003 with Q. The result is a Q-linear isomorphism Q⊗_R M_R≅T^I: tensor the coordinate maps in each direction, and identify Q⊗_R J^I with T^I by q⊗(c_i)_i↦(q⊗c_i)_i, whose inverse sums the tensors supported at one coordinate. Finite I makes these mutually inverse. An R-basis of M_R of n members, supplied by N003, extends to a Q-basis of Q⊗_R M_R; its coefficient maps extend and prove both spanning and independence. Its dimension is therefore n. Apply M001 to the finite product T^I over Q: F001 gives finite dimension, hence a finite basis and finite generation; Q has the strong rank condition by the usual finite independent-family bound. M001 gives dim_Q T^I=Σ_{i∈I}dim_Q T=nr, using |I|=n. Thus n=nr, so r=1 because n>0 by N003. By F001, θ identifies T with a one-dimensional rational subspace of C containing J. In particular, for any nonzero a∈J and any c∈J there is a unique q∈Q with c=qa.

Choose 0≠a∈J and a nonempty finite generating family g of nonzero elements of J using N003. By F002, write its members as g_j=q_j a with q_j∈Q×. For each such rational q_j, removing all powers of the prime p from its nonzero integer numerator and denominator gives q_j=p^{d_j}u_j, where d_j∈Z and both u_j and u_j^(-1) lie in R: neither the remaining numerator nor denominator is divisible by p. This is just finite factorization by repeated division of nonzero integers by p, and works for positive or negative exponents and signs. The resulting finite family of integer exponents is nonempty.

Let d be the family of exponents from F003 and set u_j=p^(-d_j)q_j, a unit of R for each index j. Let ν=min_j d_j and define b=p^ν a. Since p is prime and a≠0, b≠0. For every generator q_j a, its ratio to b is p^{d_j-ν}u_j∈R because d_j≥ν. Thus J⊆Rb. For an index attaining the minimum, q_j a=u_j b and u_j is a unit, so b=u_j^(-1)q_j a∈J. Hence Rb⊆J and J=Rb. Finally the decomposition M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i from N003 becomes M_R=⊕_{i∈I}R b e_i. These vectors span, and are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex independent. They therefore form an R-basis. Export only existence of such b, discharging the private choices a,g,q and their identities.

Every integer denominator of an element of R is prime to p, so its image in the characteristic-p field K is nonzero by H001. Thus ρ:R→K, ρ(a/b)=ā b̄^(-1), is a well-defined ring map; equality of fractions and the ring laws follow by cross multiplication. Its kernel is pR and its residue field is Z/pZ: ρ(a/b)=0 exactly when p divides a. Define φ: M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse takes (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. Both maps respect all tensor balancing relations and are inverse on pure tensors, which span. Also η:z⊗c↦(z mod pM_R)⊗c identifies M_R⊗_R K with (M_R/pM_R)⊗_(Z/pZ)K. The inverse sends (z mod pM_R)⊗c to z⊗c; changing z by p times a vector gives zero because pK=0, and all remaining balancing relations follow from ρ. These are the two natural isomorphisms of the supplied proof. H005 gives xM,yM⊆M and H003 gives h=xy-yx, hence hM⊆M. Tensoring these lattice operators commutes with φ and η by their formulas. The induced h equals h_K=x_Ky_K-y_Kx_K. The induced brackets therefore give the L_K-action, including characteristic 2.

Choose b from N004 and define B_i=φ^(-1)((b e_i)⊗1). The R-coordinate isomorphism M_R≅R^I given by the basis (b e_i) tensors to K^I; tensoring its coordinate maps gives inverse coefficient maps, proving that B is a K-basis, not merely a spanning family. Alternatively its reduction is a basis of M_R/pM_R over Z/pZ and then extends to K, via F001. N001 gives the matrices of x,y,h on e_i, and complex linearity gives the same matrices on b e_i. Their coefficients are integers, so extension along ρ and transport by φ give exactly x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for i≥1, y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for i<λ, y_K B_λ=0, and h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i, with integer coefficients read in K. Also n>0 by N001.

For every r with 0≤r≤λ<p, none of 1,...,r is divisible by p, so r! is nonzero in K by H001. Define A_r=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and C_r=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. On M the identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold; all these operators preserve M by H005. After extension they show that the induced X_r,Y_r are exactly A_r,C_r. For i,j∈I, N002 expresses E_ij as a composition of R-lattice operators and the unit binom(λ,j)^(-1). Its extension, transported by φ, sends B_j to B_i and every other B-coordinate to zero, hence is the map T_ij defined from F002. The image of that unit under ρ remains a unit and is the inverse of the coefficient binom(λ,j) in K, so this coefficient is nonzero. Substituting the just established induced divided powers in N002 gives T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) A_(λ-i) C_λ A_λ C_(λ-j). This proves every exported clause of the output without comparing reduced weights.

By N005 choose B and its matrix units T. There are n=λ+1>0 basis vectors, so V_K≠0. Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. Invariance under x_K and y_K implies invariance under their nonnegative powers and scalar multiples, so under every A_r,C_r in N005. Composing these operators and multiplying by binom(λ,j)^(-1) shows, using the N005 identity, that every T_ij preserves W. This assertion holds for all i,j∈I. By classical cases W=0 or W≠0. Under the zero branch L3: W=0, the desired disjunction holds immediately, and L3 is discharged. In the remaining branch assume L2: W≠0; then there exists a nonzero vector of W.
Choose 0≠w∈W using F001 and expand w=Σ_{i∈I}c_i B_i in the basis N005. If every c_i were zero then the expansion would give w=0, a contradiction. Thus there exists an index j∈I with c_j≠0.

Choose such j by F002. For arbitrary i∈I, the matrix-unit definition gives T_ij w=c_j B_i. By F001 this vector is in W, and c_j is invertible in the field K. Hence B_i=c_j^(-1)T_ij w∈W. All basis vectors belong to W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 and combine with the zero branch to obtain W=0 or W=V_K under L1. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. By N005 the operators are the induced lattice actions, and by H003 the integer span of x,y,h is closed under bracket; the induced action is the stated L_K-action. Its invariant subspaces are exactly the subspaces invariant under these three generators. H005 ensures these are the actions on the original arbitrary lattice tensor product V_K. Finally H001 permits λ=0 (all factorials and binomial coefficients used equal one) and permits p=2 with λ=0 or 1. None of the argument required distinct h_K eigenvalues or algebraic closure of K. This proves P in the full original domain.

roots.statement: p is a prime integer, K is a field of characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight λ and of complex dimension λ+1.
The Chevalley generators satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h, both in sl2(C) and in the action on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊆V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. No equality with the minimal lattice is assumed.

Let A be any semiring satisfying the strong rank condition (every injective A-linear map A^s→A^t between finite free modules forces s≤t). Let T be a finite indexing type, and let F_t, t∈T, be additive commutative monoids with A-module structures, each free and finitely generated over A. Then Module.finrank_A(∏_{t∈T}F_t)=Σ_{t∈T}Module.finrank_A(F_t), where finrank is the natural-number value of module rank (and agrees with finite vector-space dimension over a field).

hypotheses: A is a semiring satisfying the strong rank condition.
For every t∈T, F_t is an additive commutative monoid with an A-module structure.
Every F_t is a free A-module.
Every F_t is a finitely generated A-module.
source.statement: Let A be any semiring satisfying the strong rank condition (every injective A-linear map A^s→A^t between finite free modules forces s≤t). Let T be a finite indexing type, and let F_t, t∈T, be additive commutative monoids with A-module structures, each free and finitely generated over A. Then Module.finrank_A(∏_{t∈T}F_t)=Σ_{t∈T}Module.finrank_A(F_t), where finrank is the natural-number value of module rank (and agrees with finite vector-space dimension over a field).

source_outputs.N001: n=λ+1>0, I has n elements, and (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V. For all integers d≥0, hy^d v=(λ-2d)y^d v, and for d≥1, xy^d v=d(λ-d+1)y^(d-1)v. For all d>λ, y^d v=0. For i∈I: xe_0=0; xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1) if i≥1; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) if i<λ and ye_λ=0; he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r≤i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise.
source_outputs.N002: μ is injective. Identifying M_R with μ(M_R)⊆V, M_R is free of rank n over R, its complex span is V, and every X_r,Y_r (r≥0) preserves it. For all i,j∈I the integer binom(λ,j) is a unit of R and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ-i) Y_λ X_λ Y_(λ-j). In particular every E_ij preserves M_R.
source_outputs.N003: n>0, (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V, μ is injective, and the identified M_R⊆V is free of rank n over R and spans V over C. For every i∈I, J_i=J. The R-submodule J⊆C is finitely generated and nonzero, and M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i inside V; explicitly the map (c_i)_{i∈I}↦Σ_{i∈I}c_i e_i is an R-linear isomorphism from the finite product J^I to M_R.
source_outputs.N004: There exists a nonzero complex number b∈J such that J=Rb and (b e_i)_{i∈I}, viewed in M_R through the injective map μ, is an R-basis of M_R.
source_outputs.N005: n>0 and there exists a K-basis B=(B_i)_{i∈I} of V_K. On this basis x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for 1≤i≤λ; y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ and y_K B_λ=0; h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i. These are exactly the induced actions of x,y,h, so they define the stated L_K-action. All integer coefficients here are mapped into K. For 0≤r≤λ, r! is nonzero in K; define A_r=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and C_r=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. For i,j∈I let T_ij be the K-linear map B_j↦B_i with all other basis vectors mapped to zero. Then binom(λ,j) is nonzero in K and T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) A_(λ-i) C_λ A_λ C_(λ-j). Moreover A_r,C_r are precisely the induced divided powers X_r,Y_r on V_K.
source_outputs.P: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if x_K(W)⊆W, y_K(W)⊆W and h_K(W)⊆W, then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L_K-module, for every field K of characteristic p and every integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

R001.fact: In a finite-dimensional vector space W over a field, an indexed family of exactly m linearly independent vectors is a basis if dim W=m.

grounds.reason: H002 gives dim_C V=λ+1=n.
S002 counts I as n elements and proves independence by the displayed polynomial coefficient isolation.

R001.justification: Choose an m-element basis from the definition of dimension. Successive linear replacement inserts each independent family member into a spanning m-element family: its expression has a nonzero coefficient on an unreplaced member, or it would lie in the span of the previously inserted independent members. Solve for and replace that member. After m replacements the given family spans and remains independent, hence is a basis.

R001.fact: If (b_i) is a finite basis, T is linear, and T b_i=μ_i b_i, then T w=νw and μ_i≠ν for all i imply w=0.

grounds.reason: F002 supplies the basis (e_i) and h-eigenvalues μ_i=λ-2i.
F001 at t=λ+1 gives the eigenvalue ν=-λ-2 for w=y^(λ+1)v.
For i∈I, μ_i-ν=2(λ+1-i), a positive integer embedded nontrivially into C.

R001.justification: Write w=Σ_i c_i b_i using the basis. Linearity yields 0=(T-ν Id)w=Σ_i c_i(μ_i-ν)b_i. Independence makes every coefficient zero, and the nonzero factors μ_i-ν are invertible in the field, so every c_i=0. This is precisely the coefficient calculation used in S003.

R001.fact: For nonnegative integers a,r, r! is nonzero in C and (a+1)(a+2)⋯(a+r)/r!=binom(a+r,r), with empty product 1. This quotient is a nonnegative integer.

grounds.reason: The divided-power index r is an arbitrary nonnegative integer.
For i∈I one has 0≤i≤λ, so both a=λ-i for the X coefficient and a=i for the Y coefficient are nonnegative integers.
X_r is x^r/r! acting on a complex vector space.
Y_r is y^r/r! acting on the same complex vector space.

R001.justification: Every positive integer is nonzero in C, so each factorial is invertible. Expanding (a+r)!/a! gives the displayed product, and the usual finite binomial expression is (a+r)!/(a!r!). Its integrality follows by induction from the boundary values binom(m,0)=binom(m,m)=1 and Pascal's identity, obtained directly by putting the two factorial quotients over a common denominator. Substituting a=λ-i and a=i gives exactly S004's coefficients, including r=0.

R002.fact: If V has a complex basis indexed by a finite set of n elements, every complex basis of V has n elements. Consequently the integer basis of M supplied by H005 has n members.

grounds.reason: N001 supplies the complex basis (e_i), with |I|=n.
H005 supplies an integer basis of M that is also a complex basis of V.

R002.justification: Finite-dimensional basis comparison follows from elimination: an independent family has size at most that of any finite spanning family. In particular the H005 basis has at most n members and is finite; applying the same comparison in the reverse direction gives at least n members.

R002.fact: For a finite integer basis (m_a) of M, the map R⊗_Z M→R^n sending r⊗m to (r c_a(m))_a, where c_a are integer coordinates, is an R-linear isomorphism with inverse (r_a)↦Σ_a r_a⊗m_a. If the m_a are complex independent and R⊆C, the multiplication map to V is injective.

grounds.reason: The chosen basis is both an integer basis of M and a complex basis of V.
R is embedded in C.
M_R is the specified tensor product.
μ sends r⊗m to rm.
The basis is finite with n members, and the argument explicitly uses its coordinate maps.

R002.justification: The displayed coordinate maps are integer-balanced, hence induce maps from the tensor product. Their composites are identities by expanding m=Σ_a c_a(m)m_a and the tensor relations. The multiplication map becomes (r_a)↦Σ_a r_a m_a; a zero image forces every complex coefficient r_a to vanish. This validates the coordinate construction already given in S001.

R002.fact: For a prime integer p and integers 0≤j≤λ<p, p divides none of λ!, j!, (λ−j)!, or binom(λ,j); hence binom(λ,j) is a unit in Z_(p).

grounds.reason: p is prime and 0≤λ<p.
j∈I means 0≤j≤λ.
Any fraction with integer denominator not divisible by p belongs to R=Z_(p).

R002.justification: Each positive factorial factor is smaller than p and therefore coprime to p. Euclid's lemma, obtained from Bézout's identity for coprime integers, implies that a finite product of such factors is not divisible by p; 0!=1 covers empty products. The integer factorial identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! then excludes p dividing the binomial coefficient. Its reciprocal 1/binom(λ,j) belongs to R and multiplies it to 1.

R003.fact: Here J_i={c∈C:c e_i∈M_R} is an R-submodule. Multiplication c↦c e_i is an R-linear bijection J_i→E_ii(M_R), and this image is finitely generated over R.

grounds.reason: R is embedded in C, so complex scalar multiplication restricts to R.
E_ii is the complex-linear coordinate projection associated with the supplied basis.
J_i is the inverse image of the identified R-submodule M_R under c↦c e_i.
The e_i form a complex basis, hence each e_i is nonzero.
M_R is free of finite rank n and is preserved by E_ii.

R003.justification: Closure of M_R under addition and R-scalars gives the corresponding closure of J_i. The projection maps any vector to its i-th coordinate multiple and fixes every c e_i, proving the stated image equality. Since e_i≠0, c e_i=0 implies c=0. Writing vectors in a finite R-basis b_1,...,b_n shows that E_ii(b_1),...,E_ii(b_n) generate its image; the inverse scalar identification transports these generators to J_i.

grounds.reason: I is finite and (e_i) is a complex basis of V.
Each E_ii acts as its coordinate projection on this basis.
F001 gives E_ii(M_R)=J e_i for all i.
Every coefficient in J_i yields a vector in M_R.

grounds.reason: R is the given subring of Q embedded in C, and contains the integers.
J is the supplied R-submodule of C.
J is finitely generated.
The fraction-field and common-denominator argument is explicitly given here.

R004.justification: Multiplication Q×J→C is R-balanced, so it induces θ. Every rational is a quotient of integers in R. For finitely many tensors write q_k=a_k/s_k with a_k,s_k∈R and s_k≠0, and let s be their denominator product. Tensor balancing writes their sum as (1/s)⊗c, with c=Σ_k a_k(∏_{l≠k}s_l)c_k∈J. Expanding c in the finite R-generating family proves the spanning assertion.

R004.fact: A finite spanning family in a Q-vector space contains a basis, all finite bases have the same cardinality, and an independent family in Q^t has at most t members. For a free R-module L with basis of n elements and an R-algebra Q, those tensors 1⊗basis-vector form a Q-basis of Q⊗_R L.

R consists of fractions admitting denominators not divisible by p.

R005.fact: For the Z-module M, R-module M_R=R⊗_Z M and the map ρ of S001, the displayed maps φ:M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K and η:M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(Z/pZ)K are K-linear isomorphisms with the displayed inverses. They commute with extensions of compatible module endomorphisms.

ρ and the residue identification are established, and explicit forward and inverse formulas are given.

For η, changing a lift z by pw changes z⊗c by w⊗ρ(p)c=0; R-balancing reduces to the residue identification R/pR=Z/pZ. Its two composites are likewise identities. Pure tensors generate these modules, and applying any compatible endomorphism before or after either map gives the same formula on each pure tensor.

N001 makes I finite and supplies the integer action matrices on e_i.
S001 establishes ρ and the compatible transport φ.

R005.justification: For each basis coordinate map q_i:M_R→R, the map z⊗c↦ρ(q_i(z))c is well-defined and K-linear. These maps and the map (c_i)↦Σ_i u_i⊗c_i are inverse, by the finite coordinate expansion in M_R. This proves both independence and spanning. R006.fact: If W is a K-linear subspace invariant under endomorphisms f and g, then W is invariant under f^r and g^r for every nonnegative integer r, under scalar multiples of those powers, and under finite compositions of the resulting operators.

A_r and C_r are scalar multiples of the corresponding nonnegative powers, and each T_ij is the stated scalar multiple of a four-factor composition.

R006.fact: For a finite K-basis (B_i) indexed by I, every vector has a unique expansion Σ_i c_i B_i; each B_i is nonzero, a nonzero vector has at least one nonzero coefficient, and a subspace containing every B_i equals the whole space. In particular a nonempty basis implies a nonzero space.

λ≥0 and K is a field.
I consists of the integers from 0 to λ, so I is finite and contains 0.

R006.justification: Spanning gives the finite expansion, and linear independence gives uniqueness. If B_i were zero, its coefficient-one relation would contradict independence, since 1≠0 in a field. All-zero coefficients yield the zero vector. A subspace containing the basis contains each scalar multiple and finite sum, hence every vector.

R006.fact: If a Lie algebra over K is spanned by elements x,y,h and its representation sends them to x_K,y_K,h_K, a K-linear subspace is a submodule exactly when it is invariant under these three operators.

The displayed operators are exactly the induced generator actions and define the stated L_K-action.
